subject: Pilot cost thermometers & readiness — batching, caching, and budget gating
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@veloxpay.com>, Jared Cole <jared.cole@veloxpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot cost thermometers & readiness — batching, caching, and budget gating

Hi Samira / Jared — great conversation today. Quick written recap so we have a shared view of next steps and the economics that matter for the pilot. I kept this tight; see attached cost snapshot (velocity assumptions + per-token lines) and a short playbook for batching/caching levers.

Key pain you described
- Fraud/NLU scoring for payment flows is currently ~1.2M tokens/day during peak (batch of transactions + metadata) which spikes monthly and has pushed monthly model spend above your $15k cap.
- 95th%-tile latency requirement: <200ms for synchronous checks (affects UX).
- Security: PII-sensitive prompts — need SOC2 evidence and a private/VPC option for pilot if we move beyond POC.

Goal for pilot (agreed on call)
- Validate accuracy + latency with a production-shaped sample (10–14 days).
- Keep pilot spend under $10k/month (hard gate for this stage).
- Demonstrate 30–50% unit-cost reduction opportunity via batching + prefix/KV caching.

Preliminary economics (modelled in attached spreadsheet) — assumptions called out on tab 'A1'
- Baseline (no batching, GPT-style throughput): ~ $0.018/token -> monthly ~ $16k at current volumes.
- With continuous batching at your expected concurrency and aggressive request coalescing: ~35% token-cost reduction (mainly lower per-token GPU amortization).
- With prefix caching for templated prompts / recurrent merchant metadata: additional 10–20% effective token reduction on hit rates >=40%.
- Combined realistic pilot savings: 30–50% -> gets you into the $8k–11k/month band depending on hit rates and latency SLOs.

Operational notes / risks
- Latency trade: aggressive batching improves cost but can increase tail latency; we recommend dynamic SLO-aware batching (we can autoscale batch window at 90th percentile).
- Cache hit-rate sensitivity: benefit rapidly scales with repeatability of prompts; we’ll instrument sample prompts during the first 48 hrs to set expectations.

Attachments: veloxpay-pilot-cost-snapshot.xlsx (breakdowns), redwood-batching-playbook.pdf (implementation notes).

Next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Rafael: send cost snapshot + sample ROI scenarios (attached) — DONE (this email).
2) VeloxPay: share a 48-hour sample of 1) anonymized prompts and 2) concurrency histogram — owner: Samira; ETA: Wed 12/15.
3) Redwood: run a 48-hour simulation against the sample inputs and return an annotated savings forecast + latency profile — owner: Rafael/Infra; ETA: Fri 12/17.
4) Commercial: outline a pilot SOW with a spend cap and a reserved burst profile — owner: Marissa; ETA: Mon 12/20.

If the $10k pilot gate is still a blocker, we can scope to a narrower feature slice (async scoring only) to hit the budget while preserving a credible ROI finish. Which would you prefer as a fall-through?

Thanks again,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Rafael — this is helpful and aligns with our internal view. A couple quick clarifications before I pull the 48-hour dump: 

1) On the cost spreadsheet: can you add a line for committed-spend discount tiers (3mo / 6mo) so we can see a blended unit cost if we commit to a minimum? Our procurement team typically asks for that when a pilot looks promising.

2) Security: we'll need SOC 2 Type II evidence and an option to run in our VPC if we move past POC. Is that something Redwood supports for pilots or only for full private deployments?

3) Sizing: the $10k hard gate is firm for the pilot budget. We can carve a smaller scope (async scoring only) if the full sample pushes beyond that cap — please highlight the discrete feature-switch in your simulation.

I'll aim to send the anonymized sample and concurrency histogram by Wed 12/15 as requested. Also copying Jared (ops) who will coordinate the data pull.

FAQ/answers to prep for the prospect call

- SOC 2: marketing/legal has a SOC 2 package we can share; Rafael, please attach latest SOC 2 summary to the HubSpot deal.

I've attached the current spreadsheet and the batching playbook again for context. Samira reiterated the $10k pilot budget — if needed, we'll recommend option B and aim to surface the ROI for a follow-on commit.

Thanks — Rafael
